messages:
sophia: Heads-up: seeing a cluster of US-origin traffic routed to eu variants around 09:12 UTC. It coincides with the shadow-routing sync job. Filing here for visibility.

liam: I saw a p90 latency blip for the small-text endpoint from 09:12-09:18 (~110-130ms extra). Looks like egress+cold starts.

carol: Tracing shows requests arrived with header `x-region-affinity: us-east-1` but the chosen backend was `eu-west-1:quant-v2`. The affinity token was being dropped in some request flows.

oliver: Any policy changes recently? I changed tiered-pref ordering for lower tiers to prefer cheaper variants yesterday.

sophia: That change set the local preference cache TTL to 0 (stateless) intentionally. I didn't expect it to break affinity but maybe it did.

marta: TTL=0 forces every request to consult the global preferences which increases concurrent lookups. If updates are in flight we can get inconsistent reads and racey fallback choices.

liam: From the policy traces:
```
pref = localCache.get(key) // miss due to TTL=0
fallbacks = resolver.compute(pref)
route = planner.pick(fallbacks)
```
Concurrent misses can produce different fallback orders if global pref is mid-update.

carol: That explains why a subset ended up with EU variants. Also our route-decision metric doesn't mark cache-hits so we couldn't quickly filter these.

oliver: Quick mitigation: can we short-circuit sibling requests to reuse the first route decision for N ms? A 500ms sticky token per trace/session could preserve affinity.

marta: Short-term clamp: if a candidate route increases estimated cost > 2x and it's cross-region, prefer skipping that fallback for 500ms after a pref-cache churn.

deploy-bot: Initiating hotfix rollback: restore local pref cache TTL to 10m on policy-service in prod at 09:35 UTC. Deploy id dpl-2021729.

sophia: Rollback applied, monitoring.

liam: p90 returned to baseline ~3m after rollback, small number of stray cross-region hits still visible.

carol: I spun up a quick dashboard panel: `routing.pref_cache_hits` alongside `routing.decision.region` to correlate misses -> cross-region. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/routing-affinity

oliver: For the console rollout UX: add an explicit warning when admins set local pref TTL=0 and a checkbox to opt-in to stateless behavior.

marta: Also add a server-side guard: disallow TTL=0 in production unless `force_stateless=true` is set at org-level.

sophia: I'll open PRs: (1) add `pref_cache_miss` telemetry tag and alert, (2) server guard in policy-service, (3) patch to docs and rollout UI.

liam: I'll search recent rollout diffs for other TTL=0 usages and help sweep configs.

carol: Found 3 tenant overrides with TTL=0. Filed ENG-ROUTE-1129 in Jira and linked the configs.

oliver: Longer-term idea: automated circuit-breaker that enforces region-affinity for a short cooldown when cross-region cost exceeds threshold and cache-miss rate spikes. Expose opt-out per-tenant in console.

marta: Agree, but make it visible and reversible. Make the auto-breaker annotate the routing graph so we can audit why traffic was pinned.

sophia: Action items recap:
- rollback applied (sophia) ✅
- add `pref_cache_miss` telemetry + alert (sophia)
- policy-server guard for TTL=0 (sophia -> PR)
- rollout UI warning + opt-in for stateless routing (oliver)
- dashboard panel + alert (carol)
- sweep configs for TTL=0 (liam)
- design auto region-affinity breaker (marta)

deploy-bot: Deploy dpl-2021729 succeeded at 09:38 UTC.

sophia: Leaving thread open for 1hr to catch regressions. Ping if you see billing/latency anomalies.

marta: Good catch. We'll add this scenario to the routing postmortem patterns doc.

liam: :thumbsup:

observability-bot: Alert resolved: routing.latency.p90 spike detected at 09:41 UTC, resolved 09:43 UTC.
